name: Ilminism
summary: Ilminism, the One-People Principle, was the nationalist and anti-communist doctrine promoted under South Korea's first president, Syngman Rhee, from 1948-49 and theorised by Education Minister Ahn Ho-sang. It held Koreans to be one people of a single bloodline and destiny, rejected class, regional and sex divisions as causes of national decline, and condemned both communism and capitalist money-worship. In practice it put the nation and state above individuals and centred on Rhee's leadership.
scope: The doctrine of the First Republic (1948-c.1952) as set out in Rhee's April 1949 four principles and Ahn Ho-sang's theorisation and education policy, drawn from An's The Essence of Ilminism (1950) and from the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, Hyunkoo Kim and Wikipedia. Excludes later South Korean conservatism generally. Uses An Ho-sang's 1950 exposition The Essence of Ilminism as the primary text; Rhee's own Ilmin juui gaesul (1949) could not be opened. Scholars describe the doctrine as largely slogans, so many answers remain inferences.

Community upload of a reprint with a modern editorial introduction and glossary, which were not used.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Ilminism wanted the poor's living standard raised, but never addressed wage law and its anti-class-conflict stance cuts against mandated wage fights.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The text rejects capitalism's free or laissez-faire economy as built on discrimination and the law of the jungle, while also rejecting communist planning.

public-ownership.rationale: Kim reports a state-controlled economy, but An's text rejects communist state ownership and wants property spread to everyone; no position on nationalising industries is stated.

unions-good.rationale: Class organisation was condemned as divisive and Ahn dissolved school organisations for unity of thought, so independent unions would be suspect.

property-fundamental.rationale: The text says Ilminism 'absolutely recognises and guarantees' private property but that national interest comes before individual interest as an unchangeable rule.

cut-welfare.rationale: An wants a guaranteed minimum livelihood and the poor made prosperous, yet also warns against waiting for others to keep one alive; it is neither for cutting welfare nor for unconditional aid.

worker-ownership.rationale: Class-based demands were treated as communist-style division; economic equality was sought through the state and land reform instead.

strong-leader.rationale: Ilminism centred on Rhee as leader (yeongdoja) and was built to support strong central leadership, absolutising the leader's ideas.

state-harmful.rationale: An calls the state 'the house of the nation' and says a people without a state is as good as dead.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

reviewHistory.rationale: Anti-communism and state security came first, and the doctrine backed military reunification of Korea.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

decide-locally.rationale: An's education chapter condemns regionalism and factional spirit as the cause of national tragedy and demands one people under one state.

rehabilitation.rationale: No penal policy is documented; the ideology was punitive toward communists but said nothing on prison philosophy.

more-religion-public.rationale: Ahn drew on Daejonggyo and Silla tradition, but no programme for religion in public life is documented.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Its blood-based ethnic nationalism had no concept of remedying racial injustice; the one-people principle denies group-based remedies.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: An blames worship of Chinese culture for the nation's subjugation and wants education rooted in Dangun's Hongik Ingan and the Silla hwarang.

gradual-change.rationale: Kim says nationalism was used to keep the status quo, but the doctrine itself demanded rapid total national unification and mobilisation.

nation-first.rationale: The nation and state are the highest value; Ilminism was strongly nationalist, though it also had a pro-American tendency.

open-borders.rationale: Its one-bloodline nationalism and military unification goal contradict open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Development under state control was the aim, so limiting growth runs against it.

revolution-justified.rationale: It rejected communist class struggle and defended the established order, but its own founding was an anti-communist nation-building drive, not revolution.

central-planning.rationale: An calls for a 'unified economy' with unified planning of production and consumption, but explicitly rejects communism's coercive planned economy along with capitalist laissez-faire.

socialized-markets.rationale: It rejected both capitalism and communism but offered no worked-out market model.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land reform was a stated aim, but no tax scheme is documented.

basic-income.rationale: The text calls eating without working a crime and ties every guaranteed livelihood to work, which rules out an unconditional payment.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Kim reports development through a state-controlled economy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: An says Ilminism aims to make every poor person rich and 'to give property to all people alike', unlike capitalism's few owners or communism's confiscation.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The text guarantees private ownership and rewards work with income and property, attacking communist equal rationing as ruinous.

one-party-rule.rationale: Wikipedia notes a de facto one-party tendency, and An condemns the dozens of parties as divisive and calls on all to abandon other doctrines for Ilminism's banner.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: It sought to end formal distinctions between nobility and commoners and backed a republic.

democracy-best.rationale: An calls Ilminist politics true democracy but rejects 'fashionable democracy' as insufficient and says many selfish people speaking at will are worse than one.

direct-votes.rationale: Democracy as unified identification of the people under a leader makes referendums on laws an odd fit.

workers-councils.rationale: Class-based power bodies are the communist division it opposed.

right-to-secede.rationale: An says making one country into two violates Ilminism and that the Ilmin must stop it with blood.

natural-rulers.rationale: An says roles of leading and following differ by each person's innate ability and effort, while denying any hereditary ruling class.

political-violence-never.rationale: An says the Ilmin must stop the division of the nation 'with blood' and that destroying communism is an absolute mission.

war-builds-character.rationale: The text says nations are formed through countless fights and that Ilmin education must make people of courage, citing the hwarang who held death lightly.

separate-church-state.rationale: No formal position; Ahn used Daejonggyo-inspired myth but no church policy was set.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Nothing in the doctrine bases law on scripture; its authority was nation and leader.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state was supreme and the highest value, so privatising courts and defense is the opposite.

military-superiority.rationale: Ilminists wanted military reunification and a strong anti-communist force.

ethnic-nation.rationale: An states that one bloodline is the absolute element of the Ilmin: foreigners living in Korea are not of the nation and Koreans abroad remain so.

class-struggle-history.rationale: An's text says communism only incites envy and national division, and that the nation and state rank above any class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The Essence of Ilminism rejects communism's 'averagism' as making everyone equally poor and says pay should follow the quantity and quality of each person's work.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The doctrine was anti-Japanese in sentiment but no reparations stance is documented.

civilizational-union.rationale: Its focus was one Korean people; a broader civilizational union is not part of it.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The text faults capitalism for assuming people are selfish, and praises those who live for duty to the nation over those who live for profit.

duties-before-rights.rationale: An writes that the nation is more precious than any individual or class and that individual freedom comes only through the freedom of the nation.

restore-past-order.rationale: It was oriented to building a new unified republic and ending status distinctions, not restoring a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Essence of Ilminism says no politics can go right without theory and that one people must have exactly one guiding principle.

direct-action.rationale: Kim describes it as an establishment ideology preserving order, so extra-parliamentary action by the public is not endorsed (though state-led mobilisation was).

return-to-foraging.rationale: It pursued national development; a foraging return is the opposite.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A communist-style aim that it opposed.

distribute-by-need.rationale: An's economic chapter states that those who work well and much receive more and those who work little receive less, under a 'principle of fairness' rather than equal or need-based shares.

production-for-use.rationale: It criticised capitalist money-worship, but no production-for-use doctrine exists.

profit-exploitation.rationale: An writes that in capitalist countries the surplus of the propertyless workers' labour goes to a few capitalists, and that capitalism seeks profit without working.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: It rejected communism and class conflict outright.

collective-farming.rationale: Its land reform favoured distributing land to farmers, not collectivising it, and it opposed communism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: An states that capitalism, resting on the rich ruling the poor, necessarily becomes imperialism, and that capitalist and communist imperialisms fight each other for profit; the regime itself allied with the United States.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state was supreme and the economy state-controlled.

harm-principle.rationale: An states that Ilminism 'necessarily requires coercion' against licence, meaning any conduct departing from moral values, not only conduct that harms others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The text says individual freedom exists only through the nation's freedom and that the nation outranks any individual or class.

conscription.rationale: Its student defense corps and total mobilisation for unity support compelled service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The nation as an absolute value leaves no room for exit over voice.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is the highest value, not a service provider competing for customers.

organic-representation.rationale: Unity and anti-factionalism fit corporatism but no representation scheme is documented.

total-state.rationale: Yi Beom-seok's preface makes the nation the sole standard for politics, education, economy, culture and ethics, and An sets a unified economy and Ilminist education.

national-rebirth.rationale: An says Korea was ideologically subject to China for a thousand years and that the nation needs a new start under a new guiding principle.

territorial-expansion.rationale: An says one people should have one state and that a people holding two states would be invading others; its aim is reunification, not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: It abolished noble-commoner distinctions, though loyalty to Rhee was central.

bound-labor.rationale: It aimed to end status discrimination and carry out land reform.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: An holds that education must teach only truth and that every science studies the true laws of its object, though he also wants education to serve the nation.

universal-morality.rationale: An grounds freedom in objective moral values known by 'clear reason and pure conscience' and claims Ilminism has universality for all peoples.

single-common-good.rationale: An says Ilminist politics serves not any individual, class, sect or party but the honour and welfare of the whole nation, judged by reason and conscience.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Class-based and worker-based power is treated as divisive.

school-vouchers.rationale: Ahn centralised education in state hands for national unity, opposing school choice.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rhee's liberal-market tendency exists, but Ilminism subordinated individuals to a state-controlled economy.

rule-by-example.rationale: Ahn invoked hwarang virtue and a leader whose ideas set the standard; loosely supported.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-determination of the Korean nation was part of Rhee's state-building principles and the one-people claim.

force-without-un.rationale: Ilminists demanded marching north despite US opposition, implying willingness to act without approval.

work-for-welfare.rationale: An writes that those who work should eat and those who idle should not, and that everyone must do a minimum of work to have a minimum livelihood guaranteed.

class-collaboration.rationale: An writes that when all classes are unified as one people and work together, labour, production and consumption are unified; class division breeds communism.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: It stressed heritage such as the Silla hwarang tradition.

workers-nation.rationale: It unified classes within the nation rather than internationally, as an inference.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: An states that Ilmin morality, politics and law make no discrimination between men and women, while accepting natural differences and different tasks.

ban-interest.rationale: It criticised money-worship but no usury ban is documented.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: It had ethnic-purity elements but no law of internal racial segregation; it opposed internal discrimination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist claim opposed by a doctrine that rejected class conflict.

proportional-representation.rationale: An blames party proliferation and factionalism for Korea's ruin and demands that partisanship be abandoned; no electoral system is discussed.

national-mission.rationale: An says Ilminism will make all peoples Ilmin and build an 'Ilmin world', and Yi's preface calls Korea the signpost of a new world.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: An writes that discrimination against women erased the development of half the nation and kept education a male preserve, and calls its abolition a task still to be achieved.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: It was used to justify anti-communist suppression of the left, so accountability for past killings is opposed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The text demands that everyone's dignity and honour be respected regardless of sex, rank, wealth or occupation; membership in the Ilmin is defined by blood.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A communist argument it opposed; it does not apply.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: One-people unity and equal status support uniform law; religion was not central.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Rhee asserted democracy but the doctrine was leader-centred; Ahn held that democracy meant identification of the people with the nation.

population-transfer.rationale: It had discriminatory policies against the Chinese minority but no formal transfer is documented.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: It advocated northward reunification by force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: An writes that life is struggle and nations are 'crystals of struggle', but he rejects capitalism's survival-of-the-fittest premise and competition within the nation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: An calls the communist party the greatest enemy and demands that it be thoroughly 'exterminated'.

separated-powers.rationale: It centralised leadership, and Kim says it suppressed liberalism.

vanguard-party.rationale: A communist doctrine it rejected, though it wanted a leader-led ruling party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: An's Livelihood Economy criticises an order where the few rich prosper and the many poor cannot live, and aims to make all the poor prosperous.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The doctrine saw divisions as national decline and prized one people of one bloodline.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Security came before individuals, and the regime used the Korean War to justify suppression.

party-controls-media.rationale: Ahn sought control of thought and the regime built propaganda; media control is an inference.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Strong nationalism and national self-determination oppose pooled sovereignty.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority lay with nation and leader, not clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Internationalist class doctrine that Ilminism opposed.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral control of thought in education makes censoring harmful art plausible.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Rhee's regime later removed term limits, and the ideology served his leadership.

people-in-arms.rationale: It had student corps but also a regular army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: It opposed urban-rural discrimination but made no moral claim about rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: It demanded unification, indeed by force, as an anti-communist goal.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: It was led by an educated elite.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Its ethnic supremacism denies equal culture standing.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: It favoured sexual equality in political rights but no sex education position is known.

minority-language-support.rationale: It stressed one people, and discrimination against the Chinese community is cited.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Unity and uniform law oppose exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The text says a people of one blood and destiny must have the same thoughts and the same actions, or it becomes divided and perishes.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: It linked independence to equalising wealth through land reform.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Kim describes the state's needs over individuals and suppression of liberalism for development.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rhee pressed for direct presidential election in 1952.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A state-controlled economy opposes independent central banks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: It insisted on unification and would not concede land.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: An guarantees private property while stating that national interest precedes and outweighs individual interest as the fixed principle of Ilmin economics.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: An calls communism 'the Communist Party's monopoly capitalism', in which a few party cadres take the seized wealth and power; this is a moral charge, not a Marxist class analysis.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: An writes that splitting one country into two must be stopped 'with blood' by the Ilmin.

region-keeps-system.rationale: It insisted on one system for one people.

sacred-ruler.rationale: It did not claim divine descent for Rhee, though it exalted his leadership.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Its aim of equalising the rich and poor conflicts with flat taxes.

character-from-environment.rationale: Its blood-based view stresses heredity but its education emphasised shaping; split.

leader-cult.rationale: An's book presents Ilminism as created by 'our highest leader, His Excellency President Rhee' and calls the nation to unite under him.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform was one of its stated aims for equalising rich and poor.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Its blood-nation view and northward unification claim sit close to this.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: No documented support; no documented position, so the answer is a neutral inference from its general nationalist, state-centred principles.

women-must-cover.rationale: It demanded sexual equality in politics.

common-currency.rationale: Nationalist; the idea was not relevant.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Unitary one-people ideology opposes minority autonomy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: An argues that the war of ideas decides political, economic and military wars, and that Korea fell because it was conquered by Chinese thought, not by arms.

moral-incentives.rationale: An praises duty and moral strength but says the Ilmin state lets profit return to the worker as his own property, faulting both capitalism and communism for killing the will to work.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The text condemns hereditary upper and lower status, saying there are no separate seeds of superiors and inferiors among one people.

history-own-civilization.rationale: An criticises the old education for teaching Chinese history and customs instead of Korea's own, and calls for national education.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Anti-colonial and self-determination minded, and sought to remove Japan's legacy.

patriotic-education.rationale: Ahn's national education taught loyalty to the nation, and the book's pledge reads 'We are Ilmin: loyalty to the fatherland, love to the nation'.

delink-world-market.rationale: Pro-American; no documented position, so the answer is a neutral inference from its general nationalist, state-centred principles.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Opposed discrimination internally and put state first.

elective-rulers.rationale: An praises Silla, where the people chose the king and women could be chosen, as the origin of true democracy.

minority-veto.rationale: An demands that one people have the same thoughts and actions and be united by strict command and obedience, leaving no room for a dissenting veto.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Executive-leader centred; no documented position, so the answer is a neutral inference from its general nationalist, state-centred principles.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: An's book calls on every Korean to work, fight and be ready to die for Ilminism.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Marxist-Gramscian theory it did not use.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: It was pro-American and relied on US aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Unification-minded but not clearly about lost territory.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: It is discussed as ultranationalist and compared to fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: It opposed communism and had fascist elements; position unclear.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: An rejects imported 'fashionable democracy', says true democracy began in Korea, and wants foreign ideas digested to fit the nation's own thought.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Military security central; no documented position, so the answer is a neutral inference from its general nationalist, state-centred principles.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: State-run economy; no documented position, so the answer is a neutral inference from its general nationalist, state-centred principles.

single-official-language.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-10): its rationale calls its answer a neutral inference and admits no documented position, so the sources cited here do not answer this statement.

reviewHistory.rationale: One-people unity; no documented position, so the answer is a neutral inference from its general nationalist, state-centred principles.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-10): its rationale calls its answer a neutral inference and admits no documented position, so the sources cited here do not answer this statement.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Rejects group-based remedy; no documented position, so the answer is a neutral inference from its general nationalist, state-centred principles.

job-guarantee.rationale: An states that the Ilmin state must not only order people to work but give each person work to do; the employer-of-last-resort mechanism itself is not described.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: An writes that national unity is achieved only through 'thorough and strict command and obedience' among compatriots.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Chinese minority discrimination but no conspiracy claim.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Conservative; no documented position, so the answer is a neutral inference from its general nationalist, state-centred principles.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Thought control; no documented position, so the answer is a neutral inference from its general nationalist, state-centred principles.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereignty-minded; no documented position, so the answer is a neutral inference from its general nationalist, state-centred principles.

religious-nation.rationale: Nation defined by blood not religion.

defeat-communism.rationale: An calls destroying communism, which split the nation, the absolute mission and sacred duty of every believer in Ilminism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: An's text calls capitalism hidden materialism and money-worship and communism open materialism, rejects both economic policies, and presents Ilminism as the synthesis that supersedes them.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: An grants that capitalist policy may have suited past eras and is less bad than communism, but says it is no longer valid and blocks most people's development.

socialized-care.rationale: No documented policy on housework or child care; state-over-individual collectivism could favour public services but Confucian-tinged family values cut the other way.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Ilminism put the united people behind the leader above parties and had a one-party tendency, with communists suppressed.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The doctrine put the nation and state above individuals and classes and centred on the leader.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Ilminism rejected both communism and capitalism and claimed a third course combining their aims.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Ilminism sought to crush communism and reunify Korea by force, which needs a standing army.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: It condemned money-worship, but also subordinated the press to anti-communist national unity, so no clear stance is documented.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Scholars describe state and leader above individuals and thought control, which cuts against rule bound by standing law.

rent-control.rationale: The doctrine wanted the poor's living standard raised but never addressed housing or rents, and its state-above-individual stance gives no clear lean.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Ilminism rejected class as a basis of politics and condemned communism, so it would not accept the claim.

local-essentials-public.rationale: No documented position; the doctrine wanted the poor's welfare raised but named no ownership form.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Ilminism rejected regional divisions as a cause of national decline, so local assemblies with confederal coordination run against it.

person-over-state.rationale: Scholars describe the doctrine as putting the nation and state above individuals, centred on the leader.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The doctrine rejected regional divisions and favoured a unified people under one state, implying no entrenched regional powers.

racial-pride.rationale: The doctrine grounds the nation in a single Korean bloodline and destiny, so pride in that ancestry is legitimate.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Ilminism held Koreans to be one people of a single bloodline and destiny, so a shared language and history defining the nation, regardless of the division of the peninsula, follows from its core claim.

communal-electorates.rationale: The doctrine insisted on one undivided people above class, region and parties, so separate religious electorates contradict it.

free-public-college.rationale: No education-funding policy is documented beyond Ahn's state-controlled education aimed at national unity; the state-led economy and welfare-for-all points pull towards yes but are not specific.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Ilminism rejected sex divisions as causes of national decline and affirmed equality of the sexes, so a distinct female value claim runs against its unity stress.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Ilminism rejected class divisions and class struggle, which counts against union-versus-employer bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Ilminism wanted the poor's living standard raised but documented no tax-credit policy.

sacred-nation.rationale: It held Koreans to be one people of a single bloodline and destiny, with the nation and state above individuals.

workers-own-party.rationale: The doctrine rejected class division as a cause of national decline and demanded unity behind Rhee, leaving no room for a separate workers' party.

women-suffrage.rationale: The doctrine named equality of the sexes among its aims, so equal political rights follow.

race-social-construct.rationale: The doctrine holds Koreans to be one people of a single bloodline, which is the opposite of a social construct.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Ilminism was explicitly anti-communist, so defending a planned state with nationalised property is clearly opposed.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Ilminism held Koreans to be one people of a single bloodline and rejected regional and group divisions, so ethnic autonomy is contrary to it.

self-ownership.rationale: Scholarly summaries stress that the doctrine subordinates individuals to the nation and state, which contradicts full self-ownership.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Ilminism put the one people and its leader above classes and parties and ended partisan competition in favour of a de facto one-party state.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: No documented stance; the doctrine stressed national unity and education but is largely slogans.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: An Ho-sang's exposition lists equality of the sexes among the doctrine's principles, though divorce is not mentioned.

multipolar-world.rationale: The sources show an assertive nationalism and anti-communist alignment but no doctrine on world order.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: An wants a guaranteed minimum livelihood and the poor made prosperous, yet also warns against waiting for others to keep one alive; it is neither for cutting welfare nor for unconditional aid. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Political parties and partisan competition divide the nation and should give way to a single united people behind its leader.
missingStatements.rationale: Anti-factionalism and unity behind Rhee were defining features, ending partisan politics in favour of a de facto one-party state.

missingStatements.text: Neither capitalism nor communism offers a sound basis for society.
missingStatements.rationale: Ilminism rejected communism for class conflict and capitalism as money-worship, claiming a third balanced course.

notes: The primary text used is An Ho-sang's The Essence of Ilminism (1950), read from a scanned reprint uploaded to the Internet Archive by a community user; its modern introduction and glossary were not used. Rhee's own 1949 outline could not be opened. The doctrine is described as slogan-like and was dropped from official use after about 1952. Classification (national-conservative vs fascist) is disputed.
